section_summary: This section contains records from December 1948 to January 1949 regarding travel documentation and entry permits related to Occupied Japan. It details standing operating procedures approved by SCAP, the Department of the Army, and the State Department for extending passports and issuing travel documentation for Japanese nationals and Ryukyuans temporarily abroad. It also features correspondence and memoranda from the American Council of Learned Societies and government officials addressing restrictions on American scholars seeking entry permits to conduct research in Japan.

subfiles.about: A memorandum and standing operating procedure establishing guidelines for extending the validity of passports and authorizing travel to additional countries for Japanese nationals temporarily abroad.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Outlines procedures for passport sponsors to request validity extensions from SCAP, specifying submission channels through foreign governments or the State Department, notification of military attachés, and passport endorsement instructions.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Tokyo Despatch No. 795: Standing Operating Procedure for Extending Validity of Passports of Japanese Nationals While Temporarily Abroad

subfiles.about: A State Department circular instruction providing guidance to diplomatic and consular officers on travel documentation, passport issuance, and validity extensions for Japanese nationals and Ryukyuans.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Army Civil Affairs Division procedure for extending Japanese passports abroad, detailing SCAP policies on commercial and cultural travel, certificates of identity for emigrants, and documentation for Okinawans.
subfiles.title: Foreign Service Serial No. 951: Travel Documentation of Japanese Nationals

subfiles.about: A letter protesting restrictions that prevent American scholars from entering Occupied Japan for academic research while commercial businessmen are permitted to enter freely.
subfiles.summary: Urges the State Department to overturn SCAP's policy denying entry permits to American scholars and Social Science Research Council grantees, criticizing the disparity with commercial businessmen and emphasizing the importance of evaluating occupation policies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Odegaard to Charles E. Salzman Regarding Entry Permits for American Scholars to Japan

subfiles.about: A document file note listing attached correspondence concerning Dr. Charles E. Odegaard's representations on scholar entry permits.
subfiles.summary: File sheet listing attached letters from January 7, 1949 and February 3, 1949 concerning Dr. Odegaard.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Correspondence with Dr. Charles E. Odegaard

subfiles.about: A memorandum advising against sending a draft cable to SCAP regarding entry permits for American scholars because Secretary Royall will discuss the matter with General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Recommends withholding a draft cable on entry permits for scholars like Eleanor Hadley, noting Claude Buss's consultation, General Eisenhower's letter, and Secretary Royall's upcoming direct discussions with General MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Mr. J. F. Ray, Jr. Regarding Attached Draft Cable on Entry Permits for American Scholars

subfiles.about: A White House referral slip transmitting correspondence to the Secretary of State for appropriate acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Referral slip from White House Secretary William D. Hassett referring a matter to the Secretary of State for acknowledgment.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip to the Secretary of State
